scope: Revision 6 final decision log. All DEC-1..DEC-10 are final; UDG-1..UDG-6 are resolved; no implementation is implied. DEC-3 is clean-cutover D3-A and DEC-7 is authoritative-state/report D7-C.

decision_policy.recommendations_are: Final decisions are binding; retained prior recommendations are historical analysis only and cannot override a final.
decision_policy.final_decision_rule: All ten decisions are final only when their explicit approved decision, binding consequences, comparison/rejection record, and verification oracles are present.
authority_order: user binding direction and explicit answers
scope_constraints: This artifact proposes no source, test, config, documentation, or canonical .work-state change.
workflow_* control tools are main-session-only and were not invoked.

The host-harness steering contract is layered: host owns the safe queue/tool-call boundary and authoritative dispatch state; repository owns recovery-first policy, diagnostics, and proof-gated replay.
Research/development work is pre-planned into narrow single-owner slices; agent count follows genuine independent decomposition; attributed peer IRC collaboration and fan-in are allowed.
Manual-qa end-to-end execution remains one whole sequential scenario owner and is not mechanically split.
Workers emit concise self-initiated progress beacons at safe boundaries; parent status-pings are unnecessary. Cadence and payload must be contract/runtime-enforceable, not prompt-only.
Lost historical frequencies remain unquantified and are not numerical evidence.

DEC-1 D1-C binds the exact ordinary-mode immutable floor and the explicit durable scoped SandboxGrant night refinement: zero runtime checkpoints are allowed only inside a validated grant scope, never by blanket floor bypass; forbidden, ambiguous, expired, revoked, or mismatched actions defer durably while other reachable work continues.

DEC-2 D2-C is final: a versioned typed disjoint and closed WorkDecompositionPlan derives one candidate per simultaneously ready independent slice, capability labels derive role multiplicity, central leases cap global concurrency at 8 across nested teams and each role at 3, manual-qa remains one whole sequential owner, fan-in has exactly one output owner, deterministic later waves retain every slice, ordered compatible fallback is explicit, overrides apply last only within safety, and plan identity hashes make launched plans immutable.
DEC-3 D3-A is a clean cutover: no minimal/pragmatic/clean aliases, presets, mappings, ranking, or deprecation window; LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED blocks before planning.
DEC-7 D7-C makes compact per-run state authoritative, report projection deterministic and retained with run, event logs telemetry-only, ring latest-32, updates atomic/CAS, and redaction strict.

inputs.role: requirements, invariants, lifecycle, errors, edge cases, open decisions, and traceability
repository map, current behavior, session incident, constraints, and recovery evidence
OMP discovery/precedence evidence, alternatives, and provisional research direction

evaluated_options.name: Fixed mandatory-human allowlist
evaluated_options.material_difference: A static core-owned list defines every decision class autonomous mode can never bypass.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Auditable and durable, but requires taxonomy maintenance for new irreversible actions.

evaluated_options.name: Workflow-declared checkpoints only
evaluated_options.material_difference: Each profile/stage declares mandatory-human boundaries; there is no global floor.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Small migration, but omissions in a new profile can silently widen autonomy.

evaluated_options.name: Immutable hard floor plus contextual declarations
evaluated_options.material_difference: A small core floor is always gated; profiles add context-specific checkpoints but cannot remove it.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Final conservative balance: exact five-class immutable floor plus contextual declarations; a validated scoped SandboxGrant removes runtime asks only inside approved dev/validation scope and never bypasses the floor.

ordinary_mode_floor: cancellation/restart of a live worker whose computation may be lost
final_boundary.cancellation_exclusion: A dispatch proven not_started or failed with no loss of computation is outside the cancellation class and may proceed/retry per DEC-9 without a human floor checkpoint.
final_boundary.night_mode: Explicit durable scoped SandboxGrant; zero runtime checkpoints only in scope; floor/out-of-scope/ambiguous/expired/revoked/mismatched actions defer durably and execution continues on reachable work.
allowed_in_scope: local code writes and local commits on the bound branch/worktree
approved dev/validation deploy and health-check through project scripts
dev-domain validation with designated test accounts
reset/recreate isolated resettable dev data (seeds/fixtures) declared in the grant
forbidden_or_deferred: unknown or ambiguous environments, including indistinguishable dev versus production targets
expired, revoked, or mismatched grants/target identity

evaluated_options.name: Static roster and fixed consilium multiplicity
evaluated_options.material_difference: Profiles have predetermined slots; only roster_overrides change them.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Predictable and simple, but fails composition-driven quantity and situational staffing.

evaluated_options.name: Unbounded model-selected capability pool
evaluated_options.material_difference: A model chooses discovered roles and multiplicity from the capability pool.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Flexible but nondeterministic, difficult to bound, audit, and reproduce.

evaluated_options.name: Bounded deterministic capability-pool planner
evaluated_options.material_difference: Versioned shape signals derive bounded minimum-plus-additive slots; overrides apply last.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Meets composition requirements while keeping caps, execution authorization, and a proposed-roster artifact.

evaluated_options.name: Retire fixed tier labels immediately
evaluated_options.material_difference: minimal/pragmatic/clean disappear from option and plan contracts in one cutover.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Clean situational model, but highest compatibility and migration cost.

evaluated_options.name: Retain labels as non-authoritative advisory aliases
evaluated_options.material_difference: Legacy labels remain readable/displayable hints; context dimensions, not labels, rank options.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Preserves callers without making tiers a selector; easy to deprecate later.

evaluated_options.name: Map labels to fixed situational presets
evaluated_options.material_difference: Labels select fixed rubric weights, scope assumptions, and trade-offs.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Convenient compatibility, but recreates a hidden fixed menu and can make labels authoritative.

evaluated_options.name: Intentional load order as ownership contract
evaluated_options.material_difference: Plugin enablement/load order decides canonical ownership; first-wins is treated as user intent.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Matches observed mechanics but relies on an unverified contract and silently changes ownership on reorder.

evaluated_options.name: Reject all ambiguous ownership
evaluated_options.material_difference: Any duplicate canonical or alias claim fails instead of selecting a winner.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Strong correctness and diagnostics, but disruptive to documented challenger-skip compatibility.

evaluated_options.name: Documented precedence plus strict canonical ambiguity
evaluated_options.material_difference: Documented native/built-in/core precedence is retained; every challenger is diagnosed, and ambiguous canonical ownership is rejected.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Preserves compatible precedence without treating arbitrary plugin order as API or silently choosing an owner.

evaluated_options.name: Core engine plus namespaced bundle catalogs and aliases
evaluated_options.material_difference: One core engine/state/checkpoint/recovery contract; versioned namespaced catalogs/manifests provide host-verified hyphen aliases /do-work-<bundle>, /team-<bundle>, /cto-<bundle>, including omp.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Avoids duplicate suites and makes bundle ownership explicit; colon grammar is not claimed without host verification.

evaluated_options.name: One canonical command with runtime bundle selection
evaluated_options.material_difference: Bundles register manifests but no aliases; canonical commands select a bundle through explicit config/argument.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Clean command surface, but resolver provenance and ambiguity become central and harder to inspect.

evaluated_options.name: Independent plugin-owned command suites
evaluated_options.material_difference: Each plugin owns separate commands/config/team semantics, potentially with a wrapper or duplicate engine.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Independent packaging, but causes naming proliferation, semantic drift, and duplicated fixes.

evaluated_options.name: Immediate status-driven intervention
evaluated_options.material_difference: Silence or temporary artifact absence triggers repeated pings and possible cancellation/restart.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Observed failure pattern; starves in-flight calls and loses computed work.

evaluated_options.name: Fixed timer with one consolidated ping
evaluated_options.material_difference: A silence timer precedes one ping and bounded intervention; artifact absence alone is not immediate evidence.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Testable but cannot distinguish a healthy long call from a stall without lifecycle state.

evaluated_options.name: State-aware bounded ladder with recovery-first intervention
evaluated_options.material_difference: Running/missing artifact are normal within a bound; steering is consolidated, evidence is classified, recovery precedes rerun, and explicit abort bypasses the queue.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Best fit for the incident and recovery invariants; final under UDG-1.

evaluated_options.name: Ephemeral diagnostic log only
evaluated_options.material_difference: Mapping source/hash/fallback facts exist only in the current orchestrator log.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Low cost but poor post-session diagnosis and weak support for config-ignored cases.

evaluated_options.name: Durable state provenance fields
evaluated_options.material_difference: Latest effective mapping provenance is stored in durable workflow state.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Good resume continuity, but schema growth and path retention need redaction policy.

evaluated_options.name: Structured report plus durable redacted provenance
evaluated_options.material_difference: A shared resolver emits a report and persists redacted source, hashes, inventory, statuses, and invalidations.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Most supportable and observable; remains open pending persistence/retention choice.

evaluated_options.name: Explicit namespaced invocation only
evaluated_options.material_difference: A namespace or bundle argument is required whenever more than one bundle could apply.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Deterministic but requires command/script migration.

evaluated_options.name: Project config selection only
evaluated_options.material_difference: Canonical commands read a bundle key from project .omp config.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Compatible UX, but malformed/wrong-cwd config can silently select the wrong bundle without fail-closed diagnostics.

evaluated_options.name: Explicit override, then config, then fail-closed ambiguity
evaluated_options.material_difference: Precedence is explicit namespace/argument, project .omp config, auto only for exactly one enabled compatible bundle; otherwise candidates/provenance are returned and execution fails.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Preserves canonical compatibility without silent multi-bundle selection or a hidden picker; final under UDG-2.

evaluated_options.name: Interactive bundle picker
evaluated_options.material_difference: Canonical invocation asks the user to choose whenever namespace/config does not identify a bundle.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Discoverable for humans but non-scriptable and unsafe as an automated fallback.

evaluated_options.name: Host inbound-message queue (PX-1)
evaluated_options.material_difference: Regular steering is queued until a tool-call boundary; only dedicated abort interrupts active work.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Fixes the mechanical root cause but depends on host capability outside this repository.

evaluated_options.name: One-time guarded verbatim replay (PX-2)
evaluated_options.material_difference: A proven synthetic not-started skip may replay the exact call once after steering drains; otherwise fail loudly.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Mechanical floor for legacy hosts, requiring trustworthy state and idempotence boundaries.

evaluated_options.name: Orchestrator policy only (PX-3)
evaluated_options.material_difference: Repository waits, coalesces pings, avoids cancellation, and recovers first without changing host queue/replay.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Necessary policy but cannot prevent a host synthetic skip; final only as part of layered contract.

evaluated_options.name: Unversioned loose role/config keys
evaluated_options.material_difference: Bundles add ordinary roles/fallbacks/defaults without manifest version or compatibility envelope.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Smallest change, but stale/incompatible bundles become indistinguishable from missing agents.

evaluated_options.name: Minimal versioned bundle manifest
evaluated_options.material_difference: Manifest v1 declares identity/version, engine range, namespaced roles/fallbacks, bounded capability/required-tools metadata, min/max slots, defaults, aliases, and hash.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Strong compatibility/provenance boundary while manifest remains descriptive, not a permission or model-role system; final under UDG-2.

evaluated_options.name: Rich self-describing capability manifest
evaluated_options.material_difference: Adds detailed platform/tool/risk/checkpoint/planner/model-role metadata to the minimal fields.
evaluated_options.fit_summary: Powerful but risks schema overreach, permission confusion, and expensive evolution.

decision_log.topic: Mandatory-human checkpoint classes under autonomous mode
decision_log.question: Which exact decision classes always stay human-gated when autonomy is validly granted?
evidence: U:continuation feedback (UDG-3 final: exact floor plus scoped SandboxGrant night refinement)

options.shape: Core versioned allowlist covers irreversible external effects, destructive git, production deploy/rollback, and cancellation of a live worker.
options.tradeoffs: Low engine complexity and strong auditability; taxonomy can miss a new destructive action.
options.fit: High for hard gates, not enough for contextual variation.

options.shape: Each profile declares all mandatory-human boundaries; autonomous mode bypasses only undeclared ordinary confirmations.
options.tradeoffs: Low code cost; high omission risk for new profiles and weak proof of absence.
options.fit: Insufficiently defensive for REQ-4 without a global floor.

options.shape: Core immutable floor plus contextual profile declarations; model may classify context but cannot remove or resolve the floor.
options.tradeoffs: Medium policy complexity; explicit taxonomy risk and one shared evaluation path are required.
options.fit: Final fit for the exact ordinary-mode floor and the bounded unattended/night refinement; floor remains non-bypassable.

recommendation.reasoning: Use one core immutable floor of exactly five always-human-gated classes in ordinary and ordinary-autonomy modes, plus profile checkpoints. An explicitly activated durable scoped SandboxGrant opens a zero-runtime-checkpoint window only inside approved dev/validation scope; it never grants a blanket bypass. Floor, out-of-scope, ambiguous, expired, revoked, or mismatched actions are durably deferred in unattended mode while other reachable work continues.
ordinary_mode_floor: cancellation/restart of a live worker whose computation may be lost
recommendation.cancellation_exclusion: A dispatch proven not_started or failed with no loss of computation is outside the cancellation class and may proceed/retry per DEC-9; no-proof-no-replay remains binding.

night_mode.activation: Explicit durable scoped SandboxGrant bound to branch/worktree/session identity with allowed targets/resources/actions, forbidden actions, expiry, config/inventory hashes, and resume policy.
allowed_in_scope: local code writes and local commits on the bound branch/worktree
approved dev/validation deploy and health-check through project scripts
dev-domain validation with designated test accounts
reset/recreate isolated resettable dev data (seeds/fixtures) declared in the grant
forbidden_or_deferred: unknown or ambiguous environments, including indistinguishable dev versus production targets
expired, revoked, or mismatched grants/target identity
night_mode.defer_and_continue: Record one redacted durable deferred_action in deferred_actions/handoff before continuing the next reachable slice; never wait, poll, or idle for a human decision.
night_mode.expiry_and_resume: In-flight calls finish untouched; expiry/revocation closes the window, and resume revalidates grant and target identity before any ask-free continuation.

guardrails: Model output, hints, command variants, and task text cannot remove, weaken, or self-approve the floor or profile checkpoints.
No blanket autonomous or unattended floor bypass.
Existing dev credentials/test accounts never widen grant authority.
Unknown or ambiguous environments fail closed.
No-proof-no-replay and recovery-first DEC-6/DEC-9 semantics remain binding.

final_decision.decision: Ordinary and ordinary-autonomy modes enforce an immutable core floor of exactly: production deploy/rollback; destructive or irreversible git/filesystem/database/data/schema operations; irreversible external publish/send/payment/account effects; credential/access/security-policy changes; and cancellation/restart of a live worker whose computation may be lost. Profile checkpoints remain additive. Model output, hints, command variants, and task text cannot remove, weaken, or self-approve any floor class. A dispatch proven not_started or failed with no loss of computation is outside the cancellation class. An explicit durable scoped SandboxGrant permits zero runtime checkpoints only within its approved dev/validation scope; it allows local code/commits, approved scripted dev/validation deploy and health checks, dev-domain test accounts, Web/Desktop and Android/iOS emulator/simulator validation, and resettable isolated dev data. Production, remote push/publish, credential/access/security changes, irreversible real/external/data effects, and ambiguous/expired/revoked/mismatched grant environments/actions fail closed into durable deferred_actions/handoff while other reachable work continues.
ordinary_mode_floor: cancellation/restart of a live worker whose computation may be lost
night_mode_allowed: local code writes and local commits on the bound branch/worktree
approved dev/validation deploy and health-check through project scripts
dev-domain validation with designated test accounts
reset/recreate isolated resettable dev data (seeds/fixtures) declared in the grant
night_mode_forbidden_or_deferred: unknown or ambiguous environments, including indistinguishable dev versus production targets
expired, revoked, or mismatched grants/target identity
final_decision.cancellation_exclusion: Proven not_started or failed-with-no-computation-loss dispatches are outside the cancellation class and may retry/restart per DEC-9.

decision_log.topic: Composition signals and sizing formula for situational roster
decision_log.question: Which repository-shape signals drive slot quantity and composition, with what deterministic formula and caps?

options.shape: Keep fixed per-stage slots; expandRole and roster_overrides remain the only composition mechanisms.
options.tradeoffs: Lowest complexity and predictable resources; does not react to repository shape and fails situational sizing.
options.fit: Execution-safe fallback, not target REQ-8/10/11.

options.shape: Discover candidate roles and let a model choose roles and multiplicity.
options.tradeoffs: Flexible but nondeterministic, hard to cap/audit, and vulnerable to runaway parallelism or prompt drift.
options.fit: Can meet composition in spirit but threatens INV-3/SEC-3.

options.shape: Versioned shape snapshot yields deterministic required-role minimum plus bounded additive slots; resolve fallback chains, apply overrides last, and emit proposed roster before dispatch.
options.tradeoffs: Medium implementation cost; poor signals may under/over-size but explicit unavailable status makes it visible.
options.fit: Best provisional fit for REQ-7..11, LC-1, EC-3/5.

recommendation.reasoning: D2-C is the final bounded deterministic capability-pool planner. It plans a versioned typed disjoint/closed WorkDecompositionPlan before dispatch, derives one candidate per simultaneously ready independent slice, derives role multiplicity only from capability labels, applies compatible ordered fallback, applies roster_overrides last within the safety envelope, schedules central leases and deterministic waves, and binds the launched plan to immutable identity hashes.
contract: typed disjoint closed slice graph with one owner and one fan-in output owner
one candidate per ready independent slice
capability-derived role multiplicity; no direct signal multiplier
central global 8 and per-role 3 leases across nested teams
mandatory-risk then critical-path then phase then stable slice_id waves with no drops
ordered compatible fallback with typed unavailable/deferred
comparison: D2-A fixed roster is rejected because fixed per-stage multiplicity cannot represent genuine independent decomposition or composition-driven staffing.
D2-B heuristic/model multiplier and adaptive token/file/time sizing is rejected because it is nondeterministic, unbounded, unauditable, and tokens/time are forbidden; file counts are evidence only.

final_decision.decision: D2-C FINAL: a versioned typed disjoint and closed WorkDecompositionPlan is the deterministic slice planner. The ready independent slice graph creates exactly one candidate per simultaneously ready independent slice; capability labels produce role multiplicity. Security, infrastructure, migration, public-API, data, package, and platform evidence may create a slice or mandatory role, but file count is evidence only and never a direct multiplier; token counts, time budgets, durations, and effort estimates are forbidden. Central global leases span nested teams with a maximum of 8 live workers run-wide and 3 per role; manual-qa remains one whole sequential owner and each fan-in output has exactly one owner. Saturation creates deterministic later waves ordered by mandatory risk role, dependency-unblocking critical path, phase order, and stable slice_id, and no ready slice is silently dropped. Role resolution uses only ordered capability-compatible fallback; exhaustion is typed unavailable interactively or typed deferred unattended. roster_overrides apply last only within the discovered pool, global/per-role caps, dependency/disjointness, mandatory-role, manual-qa, and fan-in constraints; any conflict fails closed with provenance. Formula, overrides, inventory/config/selection/mapping hashes bind plan identity; launch recomputes identity and rejects drift, and a launched plan is immutable.
final_decision.formula: plan = schedule_waves(apply_overrides(resolve_fallbacks(derive_candidates(validate_graph(inputs))), overrides), central_leases); all functions are pure/deterministic over the declared inputs and canonical ordering, with execution authorization checked separately at launch.
accepted_scope: All slice-bearing research and development stages that can be decomposed into narrow independent work.
Manual-qa end-to-end remains a whole ordered scenario under one sequential owner and is never mechanically split.
Nested teams participate in the same central lease registry and do not get a private multiplier.

Execution-time discovery, disabledAgents, recursion depth, exact lookup, checkpoint policy, SandboxGrant, host queue/replay, bundle selection, and manifest authority remain unchanged and authoritative.

positive: Reproducible, auditable staffing and wave order across reruns and nested teams.
Independent decomposition drives concurrency without fixed roster waste or unbounded model choice.
Saturation is backpressure rather than silent loss, and capability exhaustion is visible.
Hash-bound immutable plans make launch drift and mutation falsifiable.
tradeoffs: Planning and durable schema work increase implementation cost and artifact size.
Poor decomposition or stale inventory can under-size work or produce visible unavailable/deferred outcomes; the planner does not hide this with a generic agent.
Global lease saturation can increase latency for low-priority slices, although deterministic waves preserve eventual admission when dependencies and leases permit.
Mandatory role and disjointness validation may reject convenient overrides and requires correction before launch.
accepted_scope_limits: No permission widening: capability discovery and plan leases never override execution-time authorization or DEC-1 floor/checkpoints.
No changes to DEC-3 tier vocabulary or DEC-7 provenance persistence; exactly those two decisions remain open.
No changes to DEC-6/DEC-9 host steering and recovery semantics, DEC-1 SandboxGrant semantics, or DEC-4/DEC-5/DEC-8/DEC-10 ownership, bundle, selection, and manifest finals.
No implementation is performed by this decision artifact.

implementation_handoff.authority: Core planner owns pure graph validation, candidate derivation, fallback status, override validation, wave calculation, identity hashing, and immutable-plan checks; bundle catalogs provide namespaced role and fallback metadata; execution and host adapters remain authorities for authorization and dispatch state.
ordered_steps: Define versioned WorkDecompositionPlan, Slice, Candidate, Wave, Lease, FallbackStatus, OverrideConflict, UnavailableOrDeferred, and PlanIdentity schemas with canonical serialization.
Implement pure typed disjoint and closed graph validation and readiness calculation; reject missing types, owners, capabilities, dependencies, IO contracts, duplicate ownership, or fan-in owners.

Implement evidence handling: permitted security, infrastructure, migration, public-API, data, package, and platform evidence can create slices or mandatory roles; record recomputable file-count evidence only; reject token, time, and effort inputs.
Implement one-candidate-per-ready-slice derivation, capability-label role demand, ordered capability-compatible fallback, and explicit preferred, fallback, and unavailable statuses.

Add one central run-wide lease registry shared by parent and nested teams; acquire before dispatch, enforce 8 global, 3 per role, one whole manual-qa owner, and one fan-in output owner; release only at terminal worker state.

Apply roster_overrides atomically after derivation and before final wave scheduling; validate pool, caps, graph safety, mandatory roles, manual-qa, and fan-in, then emit conflict provenance on failure.
Compute mandatory-risk, critical-path, phase, and slice_id waves, retain every queued slice, and reconcile planned candidates with dispatch results.

Bind plan identity to formula_version plus overrides, inventory, config, selection, and mapping hashes; refuse stale launch and post-launch mutation; replan into a new version with old-to-new provenance.
Keep REQ-6 checkpoint behavior and final DEC-1, DEC-6, DEC-9, bundle, host, and SandboxGrant boundaries unchanged; integrate planner only at the planning and dispatch seam.
Run shadow and differential comparison against the fixed roster before enabling the final planner, then verify the listed oracles and compatibility behavior for profiles without dynamic-slice stages.
required_artifacts: canonical plan_hash and six identity components
wave queue and central lease events including nested-team attribution
atomic override result or conflict provenance
failure_contracts: Unsupported plan_schema_version or formula_version fails closed; no approximation.
Graph closure or disjointness, mandatory-role, manual-qa, fan-in, pool, or cap violation fails planning with typed provenance.
Fallback exhaustion is typed unavailable or deferred and never silently substituted or dropped.
Lease saturation queues deterministically and never exceeds caps.
Hash drift refuses launch; changed inputs create a new plan; launched plan mutation is rejected.
Unattended unavailable or deferred actions use existing durable defer-and-continue semantics and never wait or poll.
migration_and_compatibility: Use M2 shadow mode and one core source of truth; retain fixed roster only as a differential baseline, not a second production planner.
Profiles without dynamic-slice stages preserve their existing artifact chains; unsupported formula or plan versions fail closed.
Keep namespaced bundle manifests descriptive and execution authorization separate; no changes to host queue or replay or sandbox floor contracts.
Roll back by disabling final planner dispatch while retaining diagnostics and static baseline; never drop the plan artifact or silently reinterpret it.
implementation_handoff.handoff_boundary: Developer implements the schemas, pure planner, lease registry, fallback, override, hash, wave, and diagnostics contracts; validation proves the oracles. This artifact does not edit source, tests, config, or workflow control state.

typed_plan_contract.graph: Every node is a typed narrow slice with stable slice_id, exactly one owner, required capability labels, dependencies, IO contracts, evidence, and one fan-in output owner; graph is pairwise disjoint and closed because each dependency names a declared slice_id or an external completed gate.
typed_plan_contract.ready_rule: A slice is simultaneously ready only when all declared dependencies are complete and its stage gate permits dispatch; readiness is recomputed from immutable plan state and durable evidence.
typed_plan_contract.candidate_rule: Create exactly one candidate record for each ready independent slice. A candidate is slice-bound and carries capability labels, phase, mandatory-risk marker, critical-path rank, fallback chain, and lease requirements; capabilities do not create duplicate candidates for one slice.
typed_plan_contract.role_multiplicity_rule: For each role r, demand_r is the number of ready candidates whose capability labels resolve to r through the ordered role catalog; role admissions are capped at 3 live leases, and additional candidates queue in later waves. No file, token, time, or model-score multiplier is applied.
typed_plan_contract.evidence_rule: Security, infrastructure, migration, public-API, data, package, and platform evidence may split a boundary into a distinct slice or mark a capability mandatory. Recoverable file counts may support the evidence record and be recomputed from a declared path or glob; they never multiply candidates. Token counts, duration/time estimates, and effort estimates are invalid inputs.
typed_plan_contract.fallback_rule: For each candidate, walk its ordered capability-compatible role or agent fallback chain against the live discovered inventory and execution-time policy. Use the first compatible available entry; expose preferred, fallback, or unavailable status and tried candidates. Mandatory exhaustion is typed unavailable in interactive planning or durable deferred in unattended mode; never silently substitute or drop.
typed_plan_contract.override_rule: After deterministic graph, candidate, multiplicity, fallback, and derived wave inputs are produced, apply roster_overrides as one atomic final roster transformation. A pin is accepted only if it remains in the discovered pool and preserves global 8, per-role 3, dependency/disjointness, mandatory-role coverage, whole manual-qa, and single fan-in owner constraints. Any conflict rejects the entire override set with formula_version, offending entry, violated rule, and derived-versus-pinned values; never clamp or partially apply.
typed_plan_contract.wave_rule: Sort all ready candidates by mandatory-risk priority, dependency-unblocking critical-path priority, phase order, then lexicographic stable slice_id. Admit candidates in that order while leases are available; candidates blocked by global, per-role, manual-qa, or fan-in saturation form the next wave. Release leases only at terminal worker state, then admit the next queued candidate in the same order. Admitted plus queued plus typed unavailable/deferred outcomes account for every planned slice.
typed_plan_contract.identity_rule: Canonicalize the formula_version, overrides, live inventory, config, bundle selection, and role mapping; compute the five corresponding hashes plus formula_version as the six identity components and plan_hash. Recompute before launch; any mismatch rejects the stale plan and creates a new versioned plan with old-to-new provenance. After launch, mutation is rejected and in-flight workers remain on their launched plan.

verification_oracles: Same plan identity, readiness, inventory, and execution policy produce byte-identical canonical plan and wave sequence.

Changing only the magnitude of a permitted evidence signal without changing typed slices or capabilities produces identical slot counts; file-count evidence is recomputable from its declared path or glob.
Any token, duration, time, effort, or hidden multiplier input is rejected as an invalid plan input.
With 8 live parent or nested-team leases, a ninth request is typed queued and global concurrency never exceeds 8; no role exceeds 3 leases.
Manual-qa admits exactly one whole sequential owner, and two owners for one fan-in output fail planning.
Ten ready slices with three free leases admit the first three in the required order and retain the remaining seven in deterministic queue order; release admits the next candidate and none is dropped.
Mandatory capability fallback exhaustion names slice_id, capability, and tried candidates and yields unavailable or deferred, never generic substitution.
A safe override yields its pinned result; an unsafe override rejects the entire set with formula_version, entry, violated constraint, and derived-versus-pinned provenance.

Recomputed identity hashes reproduce plan_hash; changed inventory, config, selection, mapping, or overrides refuse launch and produce old-to-new provenance; post-launch mutation returns an immutable-plan error.
Dispatched records reconcile one-to-one with planned slice candidates and every planned slice is admitted, queued, unavailable, or deferred with a reason.

decision_log.question: Are legacy fixed-tier labels retired, advisory, or mapped to situational presets, and who owns rubric dimensions?

options.shape: Remove minimal/pragmatic/clean from required outputs and configuration in one cutover.
options.tradeoffs: Clean steady state but high compatibility and mixed-version migration cost.
options.fit: Strong direct situational fit, weak compatibility fit.

options.shape: Accept/display legacy labels only as explicitly advisory hints; rank by scope, risk, reversibility, uncertainty, coupling, blast radius, cost, and evidence quality.
options.tradeoffs: Medium parser/rubric work; labels must never select options or become required output.
options.fit: Best provisional compatibility fit for REQ-12/13.

options.shape: Retain labels as named presets containing fixed rubric weights, scope assumptions, and default trade-offs.
options.tradeoffs: Easy migration but high semantic drift; a preset can become de facto policy and hide context rationale.
options.fit: Weak because fixed tiers drive selection.

recommendation.reasoning: Clean cutover is required; no compatibility alias, preset, mapping, ranking, or deprecation window may preserve the fixed tier vocabulary.
recommendation.non_negotiable: Core owns the eight mandatory rubric dimensions, aggregation, rationale, and safety boundary; bundle additions are versioned, namespaced, and non-overriding.

final_decision.decision: D3-A FINAL: clean cutover removes minimal/pragmatic/clean from input, configuration, state, output, aliases, presets, and deprecation paths. Any nested or persisted legacy value fails before planning with LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED. Core owns the mandatory eight-dimension rubric, versioned deterministic aggregation, and explicit rationale. Bundles may add only versioned namespaced declared dimensions; collisions and hash drift fail closed and bind plan identity.

core_rubric.rationale: explicit rationale is mandatory for the aggregate and each decision; omission or duplicate core dimensions fails validation
core_rubric.safety_boundary: core safety and checkpoint semantics cannot be changed by a rubric value

fail_closed.collisions: namespace collision or incompatible/core-overriding declaration fails before planning; no automatic rename or merge
fail_closed.version_drift: rubric/core/namespaced dimension hash drift refuses launch/resume and requires deterministic replanning

comparison.D3-B: Rejected: advisory aliases still retain legacy vocabulary and require a compatibility path; clean cutover forbids aliases, advisory hints, mapping, ranking, and deprecation.
comparison.D3-C: Rejected: fixed presets recreate authoritative tier policy, hide context rationale, and violate the core-owned situational rubric.

tradeoffs: Clean semantics and no hidden legacy selector, at the cost of an intentionally breaking input/config/state/output migration.
Core rubric governance and hash/version checks add validation work, while namespaced bundle dimensions permit bounded extension without semantic drift.
verification_oracles: Top-level, nested, and persisted minimal/pragmatic/clean values all stop before planning with LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED, field/path, and core-rubric guidance.
A valid core rubric contains exactly the eight dimensions with schema, scale, direction, versioned deterministic aggregation, and explicit rationale; missing or duplicate dimensions fail.
A compatible namespaced bundle addition records schema/scale/direction/evidence/hash and cannot remove, rename, redefine, reweight, shadow, or bypass core dimensions or safety.
Namespace collision, incompatible/core-overriding declaration, or rubric/dimension hash drift fails closed; no rename, merge, or in-place plan/resume mutation occurs.
Changed rubric or dimension hashes produce a new immutable versioned plan with old-to-new provenance.

prior_recommendation.reasoning: Advisory labels only; context dimensions and rationale rank options.

decision_log.topic: Load order and enable/disable as a supported ownership contract
decision_log.question: Can load order/enable-disable be intentional ownership, or must ambiguous canonical ownership be rejected?

options.shape: Treat plugin enablement/load order and first-wins as user-controlled canonical ownership.
options.tradeoffs: Low resolver complexity; unverified ordering silently changes ownership and is brittle under installation changes.
options.fit: Conflicts with no-silent-ambiguity requirement.

options.shape: Reject every duplicate canonical or alias claim with owner/source diagnostics.
options.tradeoffs: Strongest correctness and simple matrix tests; high adoption disruption for challenger-skip compatibility.
options.fit: Strictest REQ-17 interpretation but overrules documented challenger behavior.

options.shape: Use documented native/built-in/core precedence; diagnose every challenger/loser; reject ambiguous canonical ownership. Arbitrary plugin load order is not an API.
options.tradeoffs: Medium resolver diagnostics and staged rollout; noncanonical losers remain unavailable but every reason is visible.
options.fit: Final best fit for REQ-14/15/17, INV-7, EC-4, ERR-4.

recommendation.reasoning: Preserve only documented native/built-in/core precedence, expose all challenger diagnostics, and fail closed on ambiguous canonical ownership.
recommendation.explicit_boundary: Arbitrary plugin load order is not user intent and is not an ownership API.

final_decision.decision: Document native/built-in/core precedence; report owner, source, precedence, challenger, and accepted/rejected result for every collision; strictly reject ambiguous canonical ownership; arbitrary plugin load order is not API.

decision_log.topic: Namespace syntax, plugin specialization, and OMP-specific development bundle/team
decision_log.question: What namespace grammar and final composition of the plugin-development command/team are supported?

options.shape: One core engine/state/checkpoint/recovery; versioned namespaced catalogs/manifests own bundle roles, fallbacks, scope defaults, and host-verified hyphen aliases /do-work-<bundle>, /team-<bundle>, /cto-<bundle>, including /do-work-omp, /team-omp, /cto-omp. No duplicate suites.
options.tradeoffs: Medium manifest/resolver work and longer aliases; colon grammar remains unverified and is not claimed.
options.fit: Final best fit for REQ-14..18/23 and NG-7.

options.shape: Bundles register manifests but no aliases; canonical commands select a bundle at runtime via explicit argument/config.
options.tradeoffs: Fewer registrations but config provenance, switching, and ambiguity become central.
options.fit: Possible but weaker for explicit ownership and diagnostics.

options.shape: Each bundle owns a separate command suite, config surface, and possibly duplicate engine.
options.tradeoffs: Independent packaging; permanent duplicated checkpoint, durable, recovery, and diagnostic semantics.
options.fit: Conflicts with one core engine/state and NG-7.

recommendation.reasoning: Keep one core engine/state/checkpoint/recovery and add versioned namespaced catalogs/manifests. Register only host-verified hyphen aliases; do not claim colon grammar. The OMP catalog includes the plugin-development capabilities without a second suite.
recommendation.boundary: No duplicate engines or command suites; manifest/catalog ownership does not grant permission.

final_decision.decision: Use one core engine/state/checkpoint/recovery and versioned namespaced catalogs/manifests. Host-verified hyphen aliases are /do-work-<bundle>, /team-<bundle>, /cto-<bundle>, including omp; colon grammar is unverified and not API; no duplicate suites.
final_decision.namespace_grammar: Only host-verified hyphen aliases are decided; no unverified colon syntax claim.

decision_log.question: What is the silence window, how are steering messages consolidated, and what is the escalation ladder?

options.shape: Treat silence/missing artifact as a hang, send repeated pings, and cancel/restart.
options.tradeoffs: Simple but critical work-loss and steering-starvation risk.
options.fit: Rejected by REQ-30/32 and incident evidence.

options.shape: Wait through a timer, send one consolidated ping, then bounded intervention.
options.tradeoffs: Testable but timer cannot distinguish a healthy long call from stall without host state.
options.fit: Partial REQ-30 fit only.

options.shape: Running/missing artifact are normal within a configurable bound; collect lifecycle/tool-boundary evidence, coalesce steering, wait -> one ping -> bounded timeout -> classify -> recover -> rerun/escalate. Explicit abort bypasses queue.
options.tradeoffs: More policy/state work; waiting may delay intervention, so evidence and bounds must be explicit.
options.fit: Final best fit for REQ-24..32 and recovery invariants.

recommendation.reasoning: Still Running and temporary artifact absence are not hang signals. Ordinary pings do not interrupt active calls; cancellation requires evidence failure or an agreed bound; recovery precedes rerun.
recommendation.numeric_parameters: Configurable within this approved policy shape; not reopened.

final_decision.decision: Still Running and temporary artifact absence are not hang signals; ordinary parent/peer pings never interrupt active tool calls; collect progress/lifecycle/recoverable evidence before cancellation; cancel only on evidence failure or agreed escalation bound; recover before rerun.

decision_log.question: Should mapping invalidation/provenance be log-only, durable state, a run artifact, or a combination?

options.shape: Shared resolver emits source, hash, inventory, mapping, and fallback facts only to the current run log.
options.tradeoffs: Low cost; logs can be lost/truncated and stale edits remain hard to diagnose later.
options.fit: Partial REQ-21/22 fit.

options.shape: Persist latest effective config source, mapping hash, invalidation reason, inventory summary, and fallback statuses in durable state.
options.tradeoffs: Good resume continuity; schema/path retention and latest-only history need controls.
options.fit: Good but not a complete human-readable artifact.

options.shape: One shared resolver emits a structured report and persists compact redacted provenance/invalidations in artifact and durable state.
options.tradeoffs: Medium-high schema/redaction work; strongest supportability if secrets and personal content are excluded.
options.fit: Best provisional fit for REQ-19..22 and INV-4.

recommendation.reasoning: Use one shared resolver with compact authoritative resume state, a deterministic human-readable report retained with the run, and a bounded atomic event ring; logs remain telemetry only.
recommendation.non_negotiable: Strict redaction occurs before every durability boundary and state/report authority cannot be replaced by logs.

final_decision.decision: D7-C FINAL: the ONE shared resolver writes authoritative compact per-run resume state and a deterministic human-readable report from one accepted result. Compact state is resume/planning authority; the event log is telemetry only. Each run has one current snapshot and the latest 32 monotonic invalidation/fallback events with atomic CAS update and event-33 eviction; the finalized report is hash-bound and retained with run artifacts. Strict redaction permits normalized repo-relative paths, stable IDs, and hashes only.

authority.resolver: one shared resolver is the sole provenance authority for engine and command entrypoints
authority.resume_state: compact per-run state is authoritative for planning and resume
authority.report: deterministic human-readable projection of accepted state; retained with the run and immutable when finalized
authority.event_log: telemetry only; never authoritative for planning, invalidation, or resume

state_contract.current_snapshot: exactly one current effective snapshot per run
state_contract.event_33: append event 33 atomically evicts exactly event 1 and retains events 2..33

atomicity.update: CAS/atomic publication of current snapshot, ring append/eviction, and report projection as one version or none
atomicity.conflict: retry only against current version or fail closed; no partial snapshot/ring/report is visible

retention.report: finalized report remains addressable with run artifact identity
retention.independence: report retention is independent of telemetry/state cleanup
retention.finalization: state projection hash is recorded; later state changes create a new version rather than mutating the finalized report

redaction.outside_project: outside-project sources/paths become opaque stable ID/hash only and are not reversible from report/state alone
redaction.boundary: redaction runs before every durability boundary; forbidden values reject or replace with opaque ID/hash and no raw value persists

resume_recovery.missing_report: valid state deterministically regenerates and reattaches the report with recovery provenance
resume_recovery.stale_report: state remains authority; stale projection is diagnosed and regenerated or finalization is refused
resume_recovery.missing_or_corrupt_state: fail closed with typed resume-state error; never trust report or logs alone

final_decision.schema_compatibility: state/report schemas are versioned and additive; unsupported versions, ambiguous authority, or non-atomic migration fail closed

comparison.D7-A: Rejected: log-only provenance is lossy/truncatable and cannot support durable resume, report retention, or deterministic post-run diagnosis.
comparison.D7-B: Rejected: state-only provenance improves resume but lacks the deterministic human-readable report and run-artifact retention contract.
comparison.D7-C: Selected: combined authoritative state plus retained projection gives resume continuity, supportability, and explicit redaction/atomicity.

tradeoffs: Adds schema, CAS/atomic-write, projection, retention, ring eviction, and redaction work.
Bounded latest-32 history omits older events by design, while the retained report and hashes preserve deterministic run-level diagnosis.
A corrupt or ambiguous authoritative write fails closed rather than allowing a log/report to create speculative resume.
verification_oracles: The same resolver result produces one byte-stable state snapshot and human-readable report; changing or deleting logs cannot change planning or resume.
After 33 valid events, the ring contains exactly events 2..33 in order, event 1 is atomically evicted, sequence numbers increase, and no partial state is observable.
Repeated projection of unchanged state is byte-identical; finalized report hash is immutable and remains with run artifacts independent of telemetry/state cleanup.
Valid state plus a missing report regenerates it; stale/mismatched report is diagnosed as stale projection; missing/corrupt state fails closed and report/log alone never resumes.

A redaction audit rejects plaintext tokens, secrets, credentials, raw args, personal/unrelated content, absolute/home/traversal paths, and verbatim outside-project sources; allowed repo-relative paths normalize deterministically.

prior_recommendation.reasoning: Structured report plus redacted provenance across resume/session boundaries.

decision_log.question: Does canonical /do-work select a bundle by explicit namespace/argument, project config, or an interactive picker?

options.shape: Require a namespaced command or explicit bundle argument whenever multiple bundles could apply; canonical /do-work never guesses.
options.tradeoffs: Deterministic, but users/scripts must migrate command names.
options.fit: Strong ambiguity safety, less seamless canonical compatibility.

options.shape: Canonical commands read a bundle/profile key from project .omp config; syntax stays unchanged.
options.tradeoffs: Familiar UX; wrong cwd, malformed config, or stale mapping can hide effective bundle without diagnostics.
options.fit: Conditional on shared resolver and fail-closed behavior.

options.shape: Resolve explicit namespace/argument > project .omp config > automatic selection only when exactly one enabled compatible bundle exists; otherwise fail closed with candidates and provenance. No hidden picker.
options.tradeoffs: Medium resolver/provenance work and possible behavior change for ambiguous projects; deterministic and scriptable.
options.fit: Final best fit for REQ-15/17/21, COMPAT-1/6, ERR-8.

options.shape: Prompt the user to choose a bundle when namespace/config does not identify one.
options.tradeoffs: Human-friendly but non-scriptable; can become an implicit automated fallback or approval path.
options.fit: Not sufficient for unattended stages or recovery.

recommendation.reasoning: Explicit selection wins, then project .omp config, then auto only for one enabled compatible bundle; multiple/zero/incompatible candidates fail closed with candidates/provenance. An interactive picker is not a hidden fallback.
recommendation.legacy_config: Compatibility input may be read by the shared resolver but cannot override explicit/.omp selection or authorize ambiguous auto-selection.

final_decision.decision: Use explicit namespace/argument > project .omp config > auto only when exactly one enabled compatible bundle exists; otherwise fail closed with candidates and provenance; no hidden picker.

decision_log.topic: Steering queue primitive and implementation locus
decision_log.question: Does the host provide inbound-message queuing, or is upstream host work required for PX-1/PX-2?

options.shape: Host queues regular steering to the next tool boundary; dedicated abort bypasses queue.
options.tradeoffs: Clean work-loss fix but requires host capability and adds urgent-message latency.
options.fit: Target direct fit for REQ-28; repository consumes an adapter.

options.shape: Replay exact call once only after host proves synthetic skip was not started; unknown/partial side effects stop for manual resolution.
options.tradeoffs: Practical legacy floor; unsafe if not_started guarantee is wrong, so never unconditional retry.
options.fit: REQ-29 mechanical floor composed with D6-C.

options.shape: Repository changes only wait/coalescing/recovery policy and retains explicit abort; no host queue/replay change.
options.tradeoffs: Immediate policy improvement but cannot prevent host synthetic skip.
options.fit: Necessary and insufficient for REQ-28/29.

recommendation.reasoning: Host queue is target, guarded one-time replay is only a not_started-proven floor, and repository recovery-first policy is mandatory regardless of host version.
recommendation.implementation_locus: Repository owns contracts, diagnostics, cause classification, recovery metadata, and policy; host owns queueing and authoritative not-started semantics.

final_decision.decision: Parent/peer steering uses the safe host queue/tool-call boundary; authoritative dispatch state is accepted | started | not_started | completed; one guarded replay is allowed only with trustworthy not_started proof; no proof means no replay and loud manual resolution; repository does not reimplement host internals.

decision_log.question: Which fields are required for bundle capability metadata, required tools, roster bounds, and engine compatibility?

options.shape: Add ordinary unversioned roles, fallbacks, defaults, and aliases to existing config.
options.tradeoffs: Low initial work; stale fields and incompatibility cannot be distinguished from unavailable agents.
options.fit: Fails fail-closed compatibility and weakens diagnostics.

options.shape: Manifest v1 contains manifest_version, bundle_id, bundle_version, engine_compatibility range, namespaced role catalog with ordered fallback candidates, bounded capability/required-tools metadata, min_slots, max_slots, scope_defaults, command_aliases, and manifest_hash.
options.tradeoffs: Medium schema/compatibility work; metadata is descriptive only and must not authorize execution or remap model roles.
options.fit: Final conservative fit for REQ-16/21, INV-3/4, EC-12, LC-9, NG-7.

options.shape: Minimal fields plus detailed platform/tool/risk/checkpoint/planner/model-role metadata.
options.tradeoffs: Rich but high governance cost and risks a second permission/autonomy system or role conflation.
options.fit: Overreaches current evidence and SEC-3/4 separation.

recommendation.reasoning: Adopt only the minimal versioned envelope and bounded descriptive planning metadata. Execution-time permission, availability, disabledAgents, recursion, and model-role resolution remain core authorities.
recommendation.non_negotiable: Incompatible engine range fails closed; manifest never grants permission or remaps model roles.

final_decision.decision: Use the minimal versioned manifest with the listed identity, compatibility, namespaced roles/fallbacks, bounded capability/required-tools, slot bounds, defaults, aliases, and hash fields. The manifest is planning metadata only: it never grants permission or remaps model roles.
final_decision.authority_boundary: Core execution-time authorization, exact lookup, disabledAgents, recursion policy, and model-role mapping remain authoritative.

cross_cutting_architecture.provisional_shape: Final architecture: one core engine/state/checkpoint/recovery contract; one shared resolver with D7-C authoritative state/report provenance; D3-A core-owned eight-dimension rubric and clean legacy cutover; versioned namespaced bundle metadata; final D2-C planner; final DEC-1 floor/SandboxGrant; and final DEC-6/DEC-9 recovery-first host boundary.

migration_strategy_options.shape: Opt-in resolver/planner path compares outputs before defaulting.
migration_strategy_options.tradeoffs: Useful shadow tool but risks two sources of truth and must never become duplicate engines.

risks.risk: Mandatory-human taxonomy or SandboxGrant classification under/over-gates actions.
risks.mitigation: Immutable exact five-class floor plus profile declarations; grant scope, target identity, hashes, expiry/revocation, redacted durable deferral, and explainable failure; labels/model hints cannot remove floor.

risks.risk: Deterministic slice decomposition or live capability inventory can produce too few, too many, or temporarily unavailable candidates even though the formula is fixed.
risks.mitigation: Validate typed disjoint/closed graphs, require one candidate per ready independent slice, enforce central 8/3/1/1 leases, use ordered compatible fallback with typed unavailable/deferred outcomes, preserve every queued wave, reject unsafe overrides, and shadow-compare before activation.

risks.risk: Namespace/bundle selection changes ownership or mapping.
risks.mitigation: Documented precedence, host-verified hyphen aliases, fail-closed ambiguity, candidate/provenance diagnostics, manifest compatibility, selection hash.

risks.risk: Resolver migration leaves a duplicate reader or swallows malformed config.
risks.mitigation: One resolver for engine/entrypoints, explicit parse/missing/location/write/hash diagnostics, duplicate-read audit.

risks.risk: Host lacks queue or trustworthy not_started proof, preventing zero-lost-write behavior.
risks.mitigation: Layered host+repo contract; guarded replay only with proof, otherwise loud manual resolution; no repository-only claim.

risks.risk: Recovery replays a partially executed write or wrong slot/path.
risks.mitigation: Authoritative dispatch identity/state, durable evidence, slot/path contract, provenance, no-proof-no-replay.

risks.risk: Provenance leaks paths, project details, or secrets.
risks.mitigation: Redaction, hash-only tokens, no unrelated personal content, artifact review.

risks.risk: Compatibility-first migration leaves mixed paths with different mappings/artifacts.
risks.mitigation: Persist profile/manifest/formula/selection hashes, invalidate stale mappings, use shadow mode, retain one core source of truth.

risks.risk: Manifest metadata is mistaken for permission or model-role routing.
risks.mitigation: Minimal descriptive schema and execution-time exact lookup/disabledAgents/recursion/identity-role-model authorities.

risks.risk: No numeric anti-micromanagement values are selected and operators improvise pings.
risks.mitigation: Keep final ladder/no-cancel invariant explicit; values are configuration within it and missing values never trigger ad-hoc pings.

risks.risk: Lost historical counts are treated as quantitative evidence.
risks.mitigation: Mark frequencies unquantified; use future support tooling and first-hand mechanism evidence only.

risks.risk: Prompt-only progress beacons are missing/malformed and recreate parent polling pressure.
risks.mitigation: Runtime/contract enforcement, payload validation, missed events, and evidence-ladder input rather than immediate cancellation.

risks.risk: Night-mode scope drift or blanket bypass silently executes a floor, production, remote, irreversible, or ambiguous action.
risks.mitigation: Require explicit durable scoped SandboxGrant, exact environment/hash proof, typed forbidden list, hard expiry/revocation, durable deferred_action before continue, and no wait/poll on deferral.

risks.risk: An implementation could reintroduce a hidden roster multiplier or mutate a plan after launch while appearing deterministic.
risks.mitigation: Expose formula_version and all six identity components, reject token/time inputs, record recomputable file-count evidence only, test byte-identical plans and waves, enforce central leases before dispatch, atomically reject unsafe overrides, and reject drift or mutation with old-to-new provenance.

cross_cutting_invariants.proof_shape: The shared resolver is the sole provenance authority; state and finalized report derive from one accepted result, while logs are telemetry and cannot authorize planning, invalidate state, or resume.
Each run has one current effective snapshot and a monotonic invalidation/fallback ring capped at 32; appends and oldest-entry eviction are atomic/CAS with no partial state.
The report is a deterministic hash-bound projection of authoritative state; finalization is immutable and mismatch is a stale projection, not a second authority.

Durable state/report excludes forbidden tokens, secrets, credentials, raw args, unrelated/personal content, absolute/home/traversal paths, and unopaque outside-project sources; redaction precedes durability.
Clean-cutover surfaces accept no legacy tier vocabulary; nested or persisted minimal/pragmatic/clean values fail before planning as LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED and are never mapped or ranked.
Core owns all eight rubric dimensions and safety semantics; versioned namespaced bundle additions declare metadata/hash and cannot alter core; collisions/incompatibility fail closed.
Rubric and dimension hashes bind plan identity and resume validity; drift refuses stale launch/resume and requires a new immutable versioned plan.

known_gaps: D2-C planner implementation and runtime proof (versioned plan schema, central lease accounting, fallback, override, drift, and immutable-launch checks) remain implementation work; no DEC-2 choice is open.
Host capability detection and runtime correlation within final DEC-9.
Host verification of aliases is required before registration; colon grammar is deliberately not claimed.
Beacon runtime instrumentation and interval values require implementation proof.
Historical restart frequencies are lost and deliberately unquantified.
SandboxGrant runtime enforcement, environment-proof instrumentation, redaction, expiry/revocation, and defer-and-continue evidence require implementation proof.

autonomy_floor_constraints.name: Ordinary-mode immutable floor
autonomy_floor_constraints.statement: Ordinary and ordinary-autonomy modes always human-checkpoint-gate exactly five classes: production deploy/rollback; destructive or irreversible git/filesystem/database/data/schema operations; irreversible external publish/send/payment/account effects; credential/access/security-policy changes; and cancellation/restart of a live worker whose computation may be lost. Profile checkpoints may add gates, while model output, hints, command variants, and task text cannot remove, weaken, or self-approve any floor class. Proven not_started or failed-with-no-computation-loss dispatches are outside the cancellation class.

autonomy_floor_constraints.name: Scoped unattended SandboxGrant refinement
autonomy_floor_constraints.statement: An explicitly activated durable scoped SandboxGrant creates a zero-runtime-checkpoint window only for its proven approved dev/validation targets, resources, and actions; it is not a blanket floor bypass. Local code/commits, approved scripted dev deploy/health checks, dev-domain test accounts, Web/Desktop and Android/iOS emulator/simulator validation, and resettable isolated dev data may proceed. Production, remote push/publish, credentials/access/security changes, irreversible real/external/data effects, and ambiguous, expired, revoked, or mismatched grant/environment actions fail closed into durable redacted deferrals while other reachable work continues.
